questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had never been to Australia before and they had some exciting courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: had a lot of fun and enjoyed my time in Melbourne with lots of new great friends while keeping a high learning outcome

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not too easy, did take me some time to figure everything out. But the coordinators at Deakin are very helpfull and know the process is confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had a student orientation day

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The student coordinators were helpfull and very kind. But the process was frustrating and the website and the application didn't give too much information

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It might take a week to find off campus accommodation but it is definitely worth it. The best place to find it is through the facebook page fairyfloos

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's the best way to get to know some aussies. Deakin is an hour away with tram from Melbourne and it's a lot more fun to live in the city

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The website is a bit confusing

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have an application and you need to find information about each unit on their webpage

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As soon as i got there the student central was very helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that i wanted. had a few clashes in my timetable but since a lot was online and recorded it still worked out pretty well

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use all the help you can get and dont hesitate to email the coordinators. Dont wait till last minute on starting your application

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses is pretty much the same as at ku

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many lectures and assignments. Assignments are graded and part of your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Medical microbiology and immunology 
Wildlife conservation 
Australian Vegetation and its management
Cell Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Medical microbiology and immunology  was very interesting and we got to do a lob of cool stuff in lab. 
Australian Vegetation and its management had the best teacher and you get to be working a lot outside as well as go on a 4-day field trip which was a great way to learn and meet people

questions.answer: nothing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: groceries and beer were far more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much all the clubs and sports activities you could think of

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
In the first few weeks it's possible to try them all out, Use that to meet people and see what you like if any. 
Outdoor club is definitely worth giving a try, they arranged some very fun kayaking, snorkeling and hiking trips

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: get out of the city and explore as much as possible. Victoria has some stunning nature and flights further up the cost or to Tasmania is not too expensive. Melbourne also has so much to offer that exploring the city is a nother good way to spend some time

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, it's very similar to what we are used to

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
field trips and clubs are the best way. During classes there isn't much interactions. 
Engage as much as possible in events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: non

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and accommodating approaches of locals.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open-minded and curious 
Go to all the events 
live off campus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships that i made especially with my housemates

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: all the assignments could be a bit stressfull and you needed to be very structured

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
